title: Endocrinology Progress Note - Pump Restart Day
author: M. Feld, MD
summary: Night low 64 explained by a half-eaten dinner. BMP normal. Proceed: site-change teach-back 0800, pump basal 0815, no glargine. Breakfast bolus by pump.
body:
**Overnight**
2010 glucose 64 after a full dinner dose with half the meal eaten; treated; 118 at 2100, 132 at 0300, **138 at 0730**. CIWA-Ar stopped at 0200 (72 hours, all scores 0-2).

**Wednesday 0500 labs**
Na 139, K 4.1, Cl 104, CO2 24, gap 11, BUN 11, Cr 0.9, Mg 1.9, phos 3.4.

**Plan**
1. **0800 site-change teach-back** with the diabetes educator (new site: right lower abdomen, away from the lumpy left side).
2. **Pump basal restarts 0815** (glargine given Tuesday 0730). Settings unchanged.
3. Breakfast bolus by the pump calculator (target 120 at home). RN verifies and documents each bolus.
4. POC 1030 (2 hours after restart) and AC/HS/0300: proves the set is delivering.
5. Unexplained-high rule and pen backup in the orders. Discharge Thursday morning if the night goes well.

title: Diabetes Education Session 2 - Site Change Teach-Back, Pump Restart, CGM Alarms, Alcohol Plan
author: L. Abernathy, RN, CDCES
summary: Jordan did a full infusion set change with correct technique (teach-back passed) and restarted his pump at 0815. Breakfast bolus 6.4 units by the pump. Reviewed CGM alarm settings, backup plan, ketone meter, sick-day and alcohol rules.
body:
**Site change teach-back (0800, Dr. Feld present)**
Hand hygiene; new reservoir filled with lispro, air bubbles removed; tubing primed until drops at the tip; new site **right lower abdomen** (2 inches from the navel, no lumps); skin cleaned and dry; set inserted; cannula filled (0.3 unit for a 6 mm soft cannula); tubing looped and taped away from the belt line; old site checked. **Pump basal resumed 0815.** All steps correct without prompts.

**Breakfast 0830**
Glucose 138 (0730). 60 g: pump calculator 60/10 = 6.0 + correction (138-120)/45 = 0.4 = **6.4 units**, given by Jordan; RN checked and documented.

**Teaching (teach-back)**
- **Check the site** at every glucose check and before bed: tubing connected, no wetness or insulin smell, no redness, cannula not kinked. Check glucose 2 hours after every set change.
- **Unexplained high**: over 250, not down 1 hour after a pump correction = ketones, pen correction, new set at a new site.
- **CGM**: urgent low alarm on and loud; high alert on (250) with repeat; phone charged and not on Do Not Disturb at night; share alerts with his roommate (he agreed).
- **Backup kit and plan**: glargine pen (20 units if the pump is off for more than about 3 hours and cannot be fixed; restart the pump 24 hours later), lispro pen, pen needles, ketone meter and strips, spare sets; nasal glucagon (roommate shown how).
- **Alcohol**: eat first, lower or skip boluses for alcohol carbs, bedtime glucose 150 or higher with a snack, temporary basal reduction overnight (about 20%) after heavy drinking per his endocrinologist, never sleep with the pump tubing tangled in clothes; a sober friend who knows the plan.
- **Medical ID** bracelet: ordered online during the session.

title: Pharmacy Discharge Medication Teaching - Backup Insulin Kit
author: E. Novak, PharmD
summary: Discharge prescriptions filled (meds-to-beds at 1500 delivery): lispro vials for the pump, glargine and lispro backup pens, pen needles, ketone meter and strips, nasal glucagon x2. Storage and expiry reviewed.
body:
**Prescriptions (ordered 1300)**
- Insulin lispro U-100 10 mL vials (pump).
- **Backup**: insulin glargine SoloStar pens (20 units once daily ONLY if the pump is off and cannot be fixed); insulin lispro KwikPen (1 unit/10 g; correction 1 unit/45 above 150); pen needles 4 mm.
- Blood ketone meter and strips; glucose meter strips (backup to the CGM).
- **Nasal glucagon 3 mg x2** (home and work bag).
- Glucose tablets.

**Teaching**
- Unopened insulin in the fridge; the pen in use at room temperature up to 28 days; check dates every 3 months (his last backup pen had expired).
- Backup pens never in a hot car or the kitchen line at work.
- Glucagon: works poorly after heavy drinking (liver glycogen low): still use it and call 911.
- Copays: covered by his parents' plan.

Meds-to-beds delivery at 1500.

title: Case Management Discharge Planning Note
author: D. Kim, RN CM
summary: Discharge home with roommate Thursday. Endocrinology clinic Monday 12/21; educator phone call Friday; primary care in 2 weeks. Pump supplies on hand; meds-to-beds arranged. Work note given.
body:
**Plan**
- Home with his roommate Thursday after breakfast (roommate driving).
- **Follow-up**: endocrinology (Dr. Feld's clinic) Monday 12/21 1030; diabetes educator phone call Friday 12/18; primary care 2 weeks (alcohol follow-up, vaccines).
- Supplies: pump sets and reservoirs at home (3-month supply through the pump supplier); backup insulin and ketone strips via meds-to-beds.
- Insurance verified (parents' plan). No home health needs.
- Return-to-work note: may return Saturday 12/19 (light shift).

title: Hospital Medicine Progress Note - Day 3 (Back on the Pump)
author: A. Lindqvist, MD
summary: Pump restarted 0815; glucose 164 at 1030 and 176 at 1130 (set delivering). Teaching complete. Plan discharge Thursday morning after a night on the pump.
body:
**Subjective**
Feels well, eating normally, managing his own boluses. Embarrassed less, "more careful now."

**Objective**
POC 138 (0730), **164 (1030)**, 176 (1130). Breakfast bolus 6.4 units, lunch bolus by pump at 1200 (documented). Pump site right lower abdomen clean. Labs Wednesday 0500 normal.

**Assessment / Plan**
1. DKA resolved; back on his pump with the unexplained-high rule.
2. Hypoglycemia Tuesday evening: cause found (dose before an uncertain meal); none since.
3. Alcohol: brief intervention done; no withdrawal.
4. **Discharge Thursday morning** if the overnight glucose is stable on the pump. Thursday 0500 BMP.

title: Hospital Medicine Night Event Note - Unexplained High on the Pump (Kinked Cannula)
author: P. Raman, MD
summary: Glucose 276 at 2300 after pizza; pump correction 3.45 units; 298 at 0010 (no fall) with ketones 0.6. Jordan followed the rule himself: pen correction 3 units, new set at a new site (old cannula kinked). Recheck 0130 and 0300.
body:
**Events (Wednesday evening)**
- 1730 glucose 204: skipped the tray (roommate bringing food); pump correction only.
- 1930 two slices of pizza (about 75 g): pump bolus 7.5 units. 2100 glucose 212.
- **2300 CGM high alert; fingerstick 276.** Pump correction (276-120)/45 = **3.45 units** at 2305.
- **0010 glucose 298**: no fall 1 hour after the correction. Pizza can cause a late rise, but **blood ketones 0.6** = insulin is not getting in.

**Action (Jordan led it; RN watched)**
- **Lispro by pen 3 units at 0020** (hospital scale (298-150)/45 = 3.3 -> 3; some pump insulin may still absorb).
- **Set changed at 0030** to the left upper buttock (flank). The old soft cannula came out **kinked** at the tip (bent on insertion or when he lay on it). No occlusion alarm had sounded.
- Water 240 mL.

**Assessment**
Exactly the failure that caused this admission, caught early this time: ketones only 0.6, no symptoms.

**Plan**
Recheck glucose at 0130 and glucose + ketones at 0300; call if ketones 1.0 or higher or glucose still over 250. Discharge plan unchanged if this settles.

title: Hospital Medicine Night Note - Discharge Day
author: P. Raman, MD
summary: After the set change: 236 (0130), 168 with ketones 0.2 (0300), 142 (0600). BMP normal. Ready for discharge after breakfast.
body:
**Overnight**
Glucose **236 (0130), 168 (0300), 142 (0600)**. Ketones **0.2** at 0300. Slept after 0130. New set (left flank) clean, tubing secured.

**Thursday 0500**
Na 140, K 4.3, Cl 104, CO2 26, gap 10, Cr 0.9, Mg 2.0, phos 3.6. Weight 73.9 kg.

**Plan**
Discharge order this morning if endocrinology agrees; endocrinology to see before discharge.

title: Endocrinology Note - Discharge Readiness
author: M. Feld, MD
summary: Ready for discharge on his pump with a backup plan. He handled a kinked-cannula high overnight correctly (ketones, pen, new set). Clinic Monday 12/21.
body:
**Summary**
Moderate DKA from a dislodged pump set during a binge-drinking weekend; resolved about 27 hours after the insulin infusion started; one potassium hold; glargine bridge; one post-transition low; pump restarted after a site-change teach-back; a kinked-cannula high handled correctly overnight (pen correction and set change, ketones 0.6 to 0.2).

**Discharge plan**
- Pump settings unchanged. Change sets every 2-3 days; rotate sites; check glucose 2 hours after every set change.
- **Unexplained high** over 250 not down in 1 hour = ketones, pen, new set. Ketones 1.5+ or vomiting = call/ED.
- **Backup**: glargine 20 units if the pump is off more than about 3 hours and cannot be fixed (pump basal restarts 24 hours later); lispro pen for meals and corrections meanwhile.
- **Alcohol**: his own goals (social work); bedtime glucose and snack; CGM alarms loud; roommate knows the signs and the nasal glucagon.
- Clinic Monday 12/21; educator call Friday.
